title: Dolphin 3 — adult bottlenose in managed care: two days off fish
presentation: Adult female bottlenose dolphin under managed care has refused about half her fish for two days, is slower on behavioural sessions, and trainers report a change in the sound of her breathing.

stages.title: Assess the animal
stages.briefing: Reduced voluntary intake for 48 hours, lethargy on sessions, respiratory rate 4 per minute with an audible rattle on exhalation. Skin: two raised rhomboid plaques on the flank. Temperature not assessed. Water quality within parameters. Fish batch changed five days ago. Voluntary blood sample and gastric sample both trained behaviours.

options.label: Rhomboid raised skin plaques
options.detail: The classic cutaneous form of erysipelas

options.label: Change in respiratory sound with a rattle on exhalation
options.detail: Airway or pulmonary involvement

options.label: A 50% drop in voluntary intake over 48 hours
options.detail: Measured decline in a monitored animal

options.label: Fish batch changed five days ago
options.detail: A plausible source, but history rather than a finding

options.label: Respiratory rate 4 per minute
options.detail: Within the normal range for a resting bottlenose

stages.explanation: Managed-care cetacean medicine runs on trends, and a measured 50% drop in intake is a real clinical sign rather than an impression. The rhomboid plaques are close to pathognomonic for Erysipelothrix and they raise the stakes immediately, because the septicaemic form of that disease kills dolphins in under a day.

stages.title: Choose the tests
stages.briefing: She will present for voluntary blood sampling, gastric lavage and blowhole sampling.

options.label: Haematology with erythrocyte sedimentation rate and fibrinogen
options.detail: The cetacean inflammatory markers that move first

options.label: Serum amyloid A
options.detail: A sensitive acute-phase marker in this species

options.label: Blowhole cytology and culture with sensitivity
options.detail: Respiratory pathogens, named

options.label: Blood culture
options.detail: Erysipelothrix septicaemia must be caught early

options.label: Gastric fluid cytology, pH and culture
options.detail: Foreign material, ulceration, secondary infection

options.label: Fish batch analysis for histamine and thiamine
options.detail: Worth doing for the collection, but it will not diagnose today’s illness

options.label: Whole-body computed tomography as the first step
options.detail: Not practicable for a routine work-up in this species

stages.explanation: Cetaceans hide illness, so the panel leans on acute-phase markers — sedimentation rate, fibrinogen and serum amyloid A — that shift before behaviour does. Blood culture is on the list because of those skin plaques: erysipelas has a cutaneous form you can treat and a septicaemic form that kills within hours, and you want the diagnosis before the second one arrives.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: Haematology: white cell count raised with a neutrophilia and a left shift; sedimentation rate raised; fibrinogen 5.8 g/L (raised). Serum amyloid A markedly raised. Blowhole cytology: neutrophils with intracellular Gram-positive rods; culture grows Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, sensitive to penicillin and ampicillin. Blood culture: Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae isolated. Gastric fluid: no foreign material, mild neutrophilic inflammation. Vaccination status: last erysipelas vaccine 18 months ago.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae infection with septicaemia
options.detail: The organism from blood as well as the airway

options.label: A strong systemic inflammatory response
options.detail: Raised serum amyloid A, fibrinogen and a left shift

options.label: Penicillin is the appropriate treatment
options.detail: Sensitive on culture, and the drug of choice for this organism

options.label: Vaccination cover has lapsed and needs reviewing collection-wide
options.detail: Last dose 18 months ago against a 6–12 month interval

options.label: Gastric foreign body explains the inappetence
options.detail: No foreign material found

options.label: This can be managed by monitoring alone
options.detail: A positive blood culture demands immediate treatment

stages.explanation: A positive blood culture converts a skin lesion into an emergency: the acute septicaemic form of erysipelas can kill a dolphin in twelve to twenty-four hours, and it responds to penicillin given immediately. The vaccine interval is the finding that protects the rest of the collection and the staff, since this organism is also a zoonosis.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae from blowhole and blood, rhomboid skin plaques, raised serum amyloid A and fibrinogen with a left shift, no gastric foreign body, vaccination 18 months ago.

options.label: Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae septicaemia with the cutaneous form, on lapsed vaccination
options.detail: Confirmed organism in blood with its skin lesions

options.label: Aspiration pneumonia
options.detail: The organism is systemic and the lesions are erysipelas

options.label: Gastric ulceration with foreign body
options.detail: Nothing found on gastric sampling

options.label: Fish-borne histamine toxicity
options.detail: Would not culture Erysipelothrix from blood

options.label: Idiopathic inappetence
options.detail: Ignores a positive blood culture

stages.explanation: Naming the septicaemia sets the urgency: penicillin now rather than after further testing, intensive monitoring, and a review of the erysipelas vaccination schedule across the collection along with fish handling hygiene. Staff need telling too — this organism causes erysipeloid infections in people handling fish and cetaceans.
